mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 decline.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals robust economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a INDPRO increase > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 300,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 300,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases > 300,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% in a month signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a RSAFS decrease > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals robust construction activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth expectations improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a HOUST increase > 10%.
